InviteRow renders inline error styling and text driven by `invitesToSend[index]?.emailError`: `status={invitesToSend[index]?.emailError ? 'danger' : 'default'}` and `{invitesToSend[index]?.emailError ? (

) : null}`. This is populated as the user types, before any submit: inviteLogic's `updateInviteAtIndex` listener runs `applyInviteEmailValidation(values.invitesToSend, actions.updateInviteAtIndex)` whenever the payload contains `target_email`, and that helper calls `validateInviteRowEmail(invite.target_email, context)` with `context.memberEmails` sourced from `membersLogic`. The wiring for flagging is present in the org settings dialog's `InviteRow`. Note: the actual string-matching body of `validateInviteRowEmail` (in `inviteEmailValidation.ts`) is not included in the diff, so I cannot directly inspect the comparison, but the row-level UI and the data flow that feeds it member emails are complete and correct.

`currentInviteEmailContext()` explicitly includes the signed-in user's email in the same context object passed to the row validator: `const user = userLogic.findMounted()?.values.user; ... return { ownEmail: user?.email ?? null, memberEmails: ... }`. This `ownEmail` is passed into `validateInviteRowEmail` alongside `memberEmails`, so the own-email case is fed through the exact same flagging path used for other members, and renders through the same `emailError`/danger-styling described in c1.

Both entry points derive a submit-blocking reason from the row error: settings modal footer `disabledReason={... !canSubmit ? (inviteEmailError ?? 'Please fill out all fields') : undefined}` where `inviteEmailError = invitesToSend.find((invite) => invite.emailError)?.emailError`, and onboarding step `continueDisabledReason = ... hasInvalidEmail ? (inviteEmailError ?? 'Please enter a valid email address') : ...`. Both derive from `isValid`/`emailError` on invite rows, which the (unseen) validator sets when a row matches an existing member/own email, so a flagged row disables the batch control in both places. Per-row send control (used when email service is unavailable) is disabled the same way: `disabled={!invitesToSend[index].target_email || !invitesToSend[index].isValid}`. The exact disabled-reason wording ('must be removed') depends on the string returned by the unseen `validateInviteRowEmail`, which I cannot verify verbatim, but the mechanism for unavailability in both flows is present and correctly gated on the emailError/isValid state.

The comparison logic that would need to trim whitespace and ignore case lives in `frontend/src/scenes/settings/organization/inviteEmailValidation.ts`, which is imported (`import { validateInviteRowEmail } from './inviteEmailValidation'`) but has no diff hunk anywhere in the patch and is not shown in any 'code after patch' excerpt. `currentInviteEmailContext()` passes raw, unnormalized member emails (`member.user.email`) and the raw `target_email` into that function, so whether ' Rose.Dawson@PostHog.com' matches 'rose.dawson@posthog.com' depends entirely on code I cannot see. I cannot confirm this criterion from the given patch.

`InviteTeamMatesComponent` (shared by both the settings modal and, via import, the onboarding step) fetches members on mount: `useOnMountEffect(() => { membersLogic.mount(); membersLogic.actions.ensureAllMembersLoaded(); revalidateInviteEmails() })`. `currentInviteEmailContext()` reads `ownEmail` from `userLogic` independently of whether `membersLogic`'s `members` array has loaded (`members ?? []` degrades gracefully), so the own-email check applies even before the member fetch resolves; inviteLogic also revalidates again on `membersLogic.actionTypes.loadAllMembersSuccess`.

`reject_invite_to_existing_member` is invoked from `validate_target_email`, a per-field DRF validator run during `serializer.is_valid()` for every row of a `many=True` bulk payload before `.save()`/`create()` is ever called on any row: `def validate_target_email(self, email: str): ... reject_invite_to_existing_member(self.context["organization_id"], email); return email`. Since DRF validates all child serializers before saving any of them, one offending row anywhere in the batch fails validation for the whole request, so no `create()` (and therefore no email-sending `send_invite`) runs for any row, including ones listed earlier.

The rejection is raised inside `validate_target_email` (the per-field validator DRF attributes to the `target_email` field) with a stable code: `raise exceptions.ValidationError("A user with this email address already belongs to the organization.", code="existing_member")`. The frontend defines a matching constant to consume it: `export const EXISTING_MEMBER_INVITE_CODE = 'existing_member'` and `ApiError` already exposes `this.code = data?.code || null` and `this.attr = data?.attr || null`, consistent with a field-attributed, code-tagged error rather than a generic one.

`shouldReportApiFailure` now special-cases this: `if (status === 400 && failure.code === EXISTING_MEMBER_INVITE_CODE) { return false }`, placed before the final `return !isApprovalRequiredError(failure)` fallback that still reports other 400s/unexpected failures with different or no code. This is the shared gate documented as governing what gets filed to error tracking across API failures generally.

inviteLogic's listeners block only handles `revalidateInviteEmails`, `updateInviteAtIndex`, `showInviteModal`, `membersLogic.actionTypes.loadAllMembersSuccess`, `membersLogic.actionTypes.loadMemberUpdatesSuccess`, `inviteTeamMembersSuccess`, and `addProjectAccess` — there is no `inviteTeamMembersFailure` (or equivalent) listener that triggers a member-list refresh (e.g. `membersLogic.actions.loadAllMembers()`/`ensureAllMembersLoaded()`) when the server rejects a submission with the existing-member error. Nothing in the patch re-fetches members specifically in response to a failed `inviteTeamMembers()` call, so a member added between page-load and submit would not automatically get its row flagged afterward from this code.

result:
Inviting an email that already belongs to someone in the organization, including your own, is now treated as ordinary validation instead of a failure halfway through the batch.

The invite form only checked that an address looked like an email. The “already a member” check ran inside serializer create, so a bulk request could create and email the earlier rows before a later row rejected the request. That 400 was also filed in error tracking.

Backend: `reject_invite_to_existing_member` runs from `validate_target_email` (code `existing_member`) before any row is saved, so one known address fails the whole bulk request with nothing created and no email sent. The same check still runs in `create` for a membership that appears between validation and save. A bulk test covers an existing member and your own email in the third row.

Frontend: both the organization invite dialog and the onboarding invite step use the same rows. Typing an address that matches you, or a loaded organization member, marks that row invalid, shows the reason on the row, and blocks submit. Member emails are loaded when the form mounts, and rows are rechecked when that list arrives, so your own email is flagged even before the list returns.

Error tracking: a 400 with code `existing_member` is not reported. A plain 400 still is.
